paper_metadata.title: Variational quantum algorithm for unconstrained black box binary optimization: Application to feature selection

summary: The paper proposes a gate‑based variational quantum feature selection algorithm (VarQFS) trained with a QN‑SPSA optimizer. Experiments include a 20‑qubit hardware run on IBM’s ibmq_montreal (depth‑2 circuit with 38 CNOT gates) achieving a best test log‑loss of 0.5542 versus ≈0.556 for classical RFECV, and simulations up to 59 qubits using an MPS simulator. Results show competitive but not demonstrably superior performance compared to classical feature‑selection methods.

experiments.description: Variational quantum feature selection (VarQFS) on a reduced 20-feature credit-risk dataset, benchmarked against RFE/RFECV, using MPS simulation and IBM ibmq montreal hardware.

algorithm.variant: Variational Quantum Feature Selection (VarQFS) with QN-SPSA optimizer
algorithm.convergence_criteria: fixed 5,000 iterations for MPS; fixed 300 iterations for hardware
algorithm.parameter_initialization: initial state with equal probability mass on all basis states (uniform superposition); parameters otherwise not specified

optimizer_settings.tolerance: updates that increase loss are discarded up to twice the initial loss standard deviation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: one qubit per feature; measured bitstring indicates included/excluded feature
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize empirical training loss L~(theta)=sum_m p~_m(theta) S_train(x_m), where S_train is the model score (log-loss) of a classifier trained on the selected feature subset
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: none reported; feature subset size not fixed in the main experiments
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: implicitly defined diagonal Hamiltonian with diagonal entries f(x_j)=S_train(x_j)

problem_instance.description: Feature selection for a public credit-risk classification dataset

dataset_specification.description: 20 original attributes; 50/50 train-test split; reduced experiment uses 20 features selected as the top 20 by RFECV (log-loss) from the full dataset

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: categorical attributes one-hot encoded; train/test representativeness checked via Pearson correlation coefficients with label, requiring train/test coefficients to vary by at most about 10%
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 10 independent random seeds; 10,000 samples drawn after training to analyze subset probabilities; confidence intervals computed at 95% using 50 bootstraps with 70% of train/test data

noise_parameters.T1: reported qualitatively in topology figure; no numeric values extracted
noise_parameters.gate_error_rates: CNOT gate error rates shown in topology figure; no numeric values extracted

implementation_details.code_url: Qiskit public code referenced; exact URL not provided in paper text
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: one-hot encoding; train/test split; Pearson-correlation-based split validation
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: best sampled feature subsets evaluated on train/test log-loss; confidence intervals via bootstrapping

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: stochastic decrease with outliers; accepted updates only if they improve loss

implementation_details.convergence_data.final_loss_value: hardware training final loss ≈0.5498; best sampled train score 0.5351 and best sampled test score 0.5542

results.uncertainty: ±0.0003 (MPS average over 10 seeds); QPU best train score 0.5351
±0.0003 (MPS average over 10 seeds); QPU best test score 0.5542

speedup_claims.conditions: empirical comparison only; no formal asymptotic speedup claim
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper reports competitive or better feature-selection quality, not computational speedup.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not specified; current experiment uses 20 qubits, depth‑2 circuit (≈60 single‑qubit + 38 CNOT gates) and 300 optimization iterations.
limiting_factors: Hybrid algorithm dominated by classical model training (logistic regression for each sampled subset)
No formal complexity or asymptotic speedup claimed
Performance improvement over classical methods is marginal and dataset is small (1,000 samples)

notes: This experiment includes both MPS simulation and a real IBM superconducting QPU; the QPU run is extracted as the gate-based hardware experiment.
The paper reports 20 qubits/features and depth-2 RealAmplitudes with 60 one-qubit gates and 38 two-qubit gates for the hardware experiment.
The paper does not state a formal asymptotic speedup; only empirical comparison to classical feature-selection baselines.
Paper reports competitive or slightly better feature subsets than RFE/RFECV but does not demonstrate scaling advantage.
Problem size (20 features) is small and classical exhaustive search is still feasible.
